title: Batching thermals & kernel tuning sync - 2027-08-03
body:
Meeting: cross-team sync on kernel tuning, KV prefill thermals, and batch shaping
Date: 2027-08-03
Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Arjun Patel, Elena Ruiz, Ben Carter, Samir Rao, Ilya (remote), ops: Priya
Duration: 45m

1) Quick context and goals
- Goal for this sprint: reduce end-to-end 95/99 latency regressions caused by thermal throttling on G5-like instances during long inference tails, without sacrificing batch efficiency.
- Focus areas: kernel scheduling tweaks, adaptive batch shaping, and KV prefill pacing.
- MOTIVATION: last week's canary showed a p99 tail increase of ~22ms during sustained 80% GPU util. Need pragmatic mitigations before large kernel rewrite.

2) Observations / live metrics from canary (Jul 30 -> Aug 02)
- Baseline: same model family, sequence length distribution matched production (median 128, 95th ~640).
- Under heavy steady traffic (50qps) GPU temp rose to 84C and clocks downshifted intermittently, coinciding with p99 spikes.
- Cache prefill rate correlated with spikes: high prefill churn increased memory traffic and pushed power budget.
- Measured: throughput drop ~6% during thermal downshift windows; p99 increased 18-28ms.
- Kernel trace: observed repeated L2 cache misses on KV bridges when prefill window overlaps large batched requests.

3) Actionable hypotheses (short list)
- H1: Prefill pacing interacts badly with large batching windows; quick aggressive prefill causes memory bandwidth bursts -> thermal/clocks downshift -> latency spikes.
- H2: Kernel scheduling currently favors completion fairness which causes frequent context switches under sustained high concurrency; switching to a micro-batching affinity could reduce memory thrash.
- H3: Power/thermals are exacerbated by long-lived heavy kernels (attention matmul for long seqs); opportunistic micro-quant kernel fallbacks could smooth power draw.

4) Experiments to run this week (owners + expected outcomes)
- E1: Throttle KV prefill concurrency: limit concurrent prefill ops to 2 per GPU and add backoff when per-GPU temp >80C. Owner: Arjun Patel. Target: reduce p99 spikes by >10ms without dropping throughput below -3%. Due: 2027-08-06.
- E2: Kernel scheduling flag flip: enable micro-batch affinity scheduler on a canary pool (20 % of canary machines). Owner: Elena Ruiz. Target: lower context switch rate by 30% and observe memory bandwidth smoothing. Due: 2027-08-07.
- E3: Power-aware kernel selection prototype: enable quantized attention for sequences >512 for canary model. Owner: Ben Carter. Target: measure average power draw and latency delta. Due: 2027-08-09.
- E4: Add high-resolution telemetry (50ms) for prefill operations and attach to existing tracing pipeline. Owner: Samir Rao + ops (Priya). Target: be able to correlate prefill start/end with thermal/clocks transitions. Due: 2027-08-05.

5) Short-term mitigations (to deploy asap)
- M1: Rolling config change to add 10% conservative cap on batch sizes for CPU-bound routing tiers during high GPU temp alerts. Ops approved; ops owner Priya will push via canary flags today.
- M2: Emergency fallback: if sustained p99 > 400ms for 30s, route new requests to lower-seq model variant. Owner: Maya (implement routing rule). Target: temporary outage protection.

6) Risks and constraints
- Lowering batch sizes impacts unit cost; need to quantify cost delta if mitigation becomes long-term. Finance visibility required if mitigation persists >2 weeks.
- Kernel changes may require ABI compatibility checks for private deployments. Catalog team must be notified before shipping any kernel selector changes.

7) Discussion notes (key points)
- Arjun: initial profiling indicates prefill churn is the single largest spike contributor; pacing may yield immediate wins.
- Elena: scheduler change has moderate complexity but good signal in lab. She recommends micro-batch affinity default only on machines with single tenant loads (dedicated pools).
- Ben: quantized attention fallback reduced power draw by ~12% in offline sim at the cost of +6ms median latency; acceptable as an emergency smoothing option.
- Samir: telemetry addition is urgent — current 1s sampling misses short bursts. 50ms granularity should make correlations much clearer.
- Ilya: suggested we add an integration smoke test that simulates sustained prefill + burst loads to catch regressions earlier in CI.

8) Decisions made
- Proceed in parallel with E1, E2, E4 this week. Fast-follow E3 if E1/E2 don't meet targets.
- Deploy M1 immediately to canary routing pool; M2 to be enabled as an emergency safety net with a 1h on-call rollback playbook.
- Notify product and the catalog team of potential longer-term kernel selector changes.

9) Concrete next steps & owners (copy for Slack update)
- Arjun: implement KV prefill concurrency limiter + temp-based backoff; run canary; post results in #serving-runtime by EOD 2027-08-06.
- Elena: spin up scheduler-canary (20% pool), enable micro-batch affinity, collect traces; update PR in GH. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/1543. Due 2027-08-07.
- Ben: enable attention-quant-fallback in offline sim and prepare quick toggle for canary if needed. Share numbers by 2027-08-08.
- Samir & Priya: rollout high-res telemetry and add dashboards. Smoke tests for correlation added to nightly. Due 2027-08-05.
- Maya: prepare a one-pager for product/finance describing mitigation cost impact and thresholds for escalation. Due 2027-08-09.

10) Notes to self / loose thoughts (brainstorm style)
- Would be useful to run a thermal-aware scheduler experiment that includes a small prediction window (predict temp 5s ahead using short-term moving average of memory bw) and preempt heavy kernels.
- Consider adding a GPU-side tokenized workload shedding mechanism at the runtime level (if cache prefill plus large batch cause sustained power draw, temporarily shed non-critical prefill ops).
- Longer-term: kernel rewrite to reduce memory copy steps in KV bridge; big task but could remove a key thrash point. Raise to roadmap if experiments show clear ROI.

Appendix: raw metrics snapshot (selected)
- Canary pool (n=12 GPUs) median util: 78% (stdev 6%)
- Avg power draw baseline: 315W; during spikes 345W
- p50/p95/p99 baseline: 9ms / 42ms / 112ms
- p50/p95/p99 during spike windows: 11ms / 57ms / 140ms
- Prefill concurrency observed: bursts of 6-10 concurrent ops per GPU
- Memory bandwidth observed during bursts: +22% over baseline

If anything urgent arises, ping Maya or post in #serving-runtime. Will reconvene next Tuesday checkpoint to evaluate experiment outcomes and decide on follow-ups.
